Make tables and fit survey models

Source: vignettes/articles/tables-and-models.Rmd
tables-and-models.Rmd
library(easyNIS)
library(dplyr)
library(srvyr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

The examples use invented data.

Summarize the cohort 

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50")
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmpt5gwgk/duckdb

#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.

#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/Rtmpt5gwgk/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
design <- nis_design(nis, AGE >= 18, keep = c(AGE, LOS, DIED, RACE, heart_failure))
#> Preparing the cohort survey design.

design |>
  group_by(heart_failure) |>
  summarise(
    sampled = unweighted(n()),
    discharge_total = survey_total(),
    mean_los = survey_mean(LOS, na.rm = TRUE, vartype = c("se", "ci"))
  )
#> # A tibble: 2 × 8
#>   heart_failure sampled discharge_total discharge_total_se mean_los mean_los_se
#>   <lgl>           <int>           <dbl>              <dbl>    <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 FALSE              84            104                19.9     5.38       0.273
#> 2 TRUE              108            125.               17.3     5.66       0.229
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: mean_los_low <dbl>, mean_los_upp <dbl>

sampled counts records. discharge_total estimates the number of discharges across both years. Set the denominator for each statistic before reviewing its disclosure risk.

Install gtsummary and cardx for the survey table, and broom.helpers for the regression table below.

library(gtsummary)

table_design <- design |> select(YEAR, HOSP_NIS, heart_failure, AGE, LOS, DIED)
tbl_svysummary(table_design, by = heart_failure, include = c(AGE, LOS, DIED)) |>
  nis_suppress()
Characteristic TRUE
N = 1251,2 		FALSE
N = 1041,2
Age, years 59 (41, 76) 65 (49, 77)
Length of stay, days 6.0 (3.0, 9.0) 5.0 (2.0, 8.0)
Died during hospitalization ≤10 ≤10
1 Median (Q1, Q3); n (%)
2 Statistics based on unweighted n ≤10 are marked ≤10; cells contributed by fewer than two distinct year-scoped hospitals are marked '<2 hospitals', regardless of count. The discharge-count mask takes precedence when both rules apply. Dichotomous rows with a protected complement are marked 'Masked' when the displayed event passes both rules. When a categorical variable has one masked level in a column, the smallest remaining positive level is marked 'Masked'. Before sharing under the HCUP Data Use Agreement, review tables for other derivable cells.

Select the table’s variables before building it. Keep YEAR and HOSP_NIS so suppression can count contributing hospital-years. Reuse the original design for models that need additional variables.

Fit a model and estimate a contrast 

fit <- survey::svyglm(LOS ~ heart_failure + AGE, design = design)
survey::svycontrast(fit, c(heart_failureTRUE = 1))
#>          contrast     SE
#> contrast  0.17863 0.4205
tbl_regression(fit)
Characteristic Beta 95% CI p-value
heart_failure


    FALSE — —
    TRUE 0.18 -0.71, 1.1 0.7
Age, years -0.02 -0.04, -0.01 0.001
Abbreviation: CI = Confidence Interval 
nobs(fit)
#> [1] 192

The contrast estimates the adjusted difference in mean length of stay. Use the fitted model’s count to report the number of sampled discharges. The N returned through tbl_regression() for a svyglm() can be weighted. Check the fitted sample before labeling or reporting N. Check disclosure

Report weighted event rates

To report in-hospital mortality among adults under age 65, filter the survey design so hospitals with no discharges in the domain still contribute to variance estimation. Here the rates and the model use the same complete cases. Include any additional model covariates in the missing-value checks if you want both analyses to use the same discharges.

mortality_design <- design |>
  filter(AGE < 65, !is.na(DIED), !is.na(heart_failure))
design_df <- survey::degf(mortality_design)

rates <- mortality_design |>
  group_by(heart_failure) |>
  summarise(
    events_sampled = unweighted(sum(DIED)),
    discharges_sampled = unweighted(n()),
    events_weighted = survey_total(DIED, vartype = NULL),
    discharges_weighted = survey_total(vartype = NULL),
    rate = survey_mean(DIED, vartype = c("se", "ci"), df = design_df)
  )

The rate is the weighted share of discharges with an in-hospital death. The sampled columns count observed deaths and discharges. The weighted columns estimate their totals over the years in the design. The rate, standard error, and 95% confidence limits are on the 0–1 scale.

Before displaying the rates or their counts, check support for both deaths and discharges without a death. An absent outcome level has zero support. Mask the rate, its uncertainty, and all counts together when either outcome level is protected.

support <- nis_cell_counts(mortality_design, by = c(heart_failure, DIED)) |>
  group_by(heart_failure) |>
  summarise(
    min_sampled = if (n() == 2L) min(n) else 0L,
    min_hospitals = if (n() == 2L) min(hospitals) else 0L,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

rates_for_review <- rates |>
  left_join(support, by = "heart_failure") |>
  nis_suppress(
    count_col = min_sampled,
    hospital_col = min_hospitals,
    weighted_cols = c(events_sampled, discharges_sampled, events_weighted,
                      discharges_weighted, rate, rate_se, rate_low, rate_upp)
  ) |>
  select(-min_sampled, -min_hospitals)
rates_for_review
#> # A tibble: 2 × 9
#>   heart_failure events_sampled discharges_sampled events_weighted
#>   <lgl>         <chr>          <chr>              <chr>          
#> 1 FALSE         ≤10            ≤10                ≤10            
#> 2 TRUE          ≤10            ≤10                ≤10            
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: discharges_weighted <chr>, rate <chr>, rate_se <chr>,
#> #   rate_low <chr>, rate_upp <chr>

Complementary suppression is on by default: if one exposure group is masked, a second group is masked too, so the masked group can’t be recovered from the cohort total reported elsewhere. Still review overlapping tables, totals, and contrasts for deductions from masked cells before sharing. See disclosure review.

Estimate adjusted probabilities and a reference difference

survey::svypredmeans() takes an adjustment model whose formula omits the exposure. It adds the exposure as a main effect, then averages the predicted probabilities at each exposure level over the same weighted age distribution in the analytic domain. survey::svycontrast() uses the covariance of the margins to estimate the difference from the no-heart-failure reference.

adjustment <- survey::svyglm(
  DIED ~ AGE,
  design = mortality_design,
  family = quasibinomial()
)
margins <- survey::svypredmeans(
  adjustment, ~heart_failure, predictat = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
estimates <- survey::svycontrast(
  margins,
  list(
    "No heart failure" = c("FALSE" = 1),
    "Heart failure" = c("TRUE" = 1),
    "Difference vs. no heart failure" = c("FALSE" = -1, "TRUE" = 1)
  )
)
limits <- confint(estimates, df = design_df)
adjusted <- tibble::tibble(
  term = names(coef(estimates)),
  estimate = as.numeric(coef(estimates)),
  std.error = as.numeric(survey::SE(estimates)),
  conf.low = limits[, 1],
  conf.high = limits[, 2]
)
adjusted
#> # A tibble: 3 × 5
#>   term                            estimate std.error conf.low conf.high
#>   <chr>                              <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 No heart failure                  0.0515    0.0284 -0.00814    0.111 
#> 2 Heart failure                     0.0285    0.0210 -0.0157     0.0727
#> 3 Difference vs. no heart failure  -0.0230    0.0415 -0.110      0.0642

Multiply the difference by 100 to report percentage points. The adjusted probabilities and contrast above are for invented data. Before reporting results from a study, check the outcome and exposure cells in the fitted sample and assess what the predictions and contrast could reveal together with the other outputs.

Apply prespecified reweights 

reweighted <- nis_reweight(design, ifelse(AGE >= 65, 1.2, 0.9))
summarise(reweighted, mean_los = survey_mean(LOS))
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   mean_los mean_los_se
#>      <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1     5.41       0.151

These factors illustrate how to apply multipliers. In a study, define the target population and assess overlap and balance for the chosen weighting method. The standard errors treat the supplied factors as fixed. Use the original design for national discharge counts. Multiplying by analysis weights changes what the totals estimate. Annualization alone divides every design weight by the same number of years.
